title: Intermittent kernel preemption leak causing TTFT tail spikes and tokens/sec collapse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported severe TTFT tail spikes and dramatic tokens/sec drops across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after 2025-02-16 runtime rollout. Initial traces point to a kernel preemption path that intermittently leaks execution tokens from the multiplex scheduler, causing worker starvation on long-context and burst workloads.
incident_summary: From 2025-02-17 03:00 UTC we started receiving escalations from three customers (AcmeHealth, NovaDocs, and LedgerAI) reporting >5x initial token latency and throughput collapse to <10% expected tokens/sec on certain model families and sequence lengths. The issue reproduced in hosted and private stacks, indicating a common runtime regression. Telemetry showed a correlated increase in preemption counts and KV cache churn on affected hosts.
steps_taken: 2025-02-17 04:10 UTC: Triage call with oncall, SRE, and runtime team to collect traces and affected host list
Captured heap and scheduler metrics from impacted workers and compared with baseline from 2025-02-15
Reproduced tokens/sec collapse in a controlled test harness by replaying customer request traces with long prefix lengths
Added temporary request-level routing rule to route impacted tenant traffic to fallback kernel variant (kernel-v1.18-compat) to reduce customer severity
Instrumented scheduler to emit preemption stack traces and per-request preempt counts to narrow leak location
investigation_findings: Root cause narrowed to a race in kernel preemption bookkeeping where canceled preemption timers were not clearing a per-worker token credit, leading to slow accumulation of orphaned credits and delayed wakeups. This manifested under high fanout of multi-model requests and when KV cache eviction churn was high.
hotfix_plan: Backport a deterministic fix that clears preemption credits on cancel and adds a periodic scavenger that reclaims orphaned credits after 30s. Deploy hotfix to a canary pool of 10% capacity in Hosted, then push to Dedicated zones with active customers, then Private customers via customer-specific upgrade bundles.
deploy_plan: Build runtime-1.19.1-hotfix branch with preemption-credit-fix and scavenger
Run end-to-end perf regression suite with long-context replay and KV churn profiles (baseline vs hotfix)
Deploy to Hosted canary (10%) and monitor TTFT, tokens/sec, preemption-count metrics for 1 hour
If stable, schedule staggered rollout to remaining Hosted capacity and Dedicated zones over next 6 hours
Coordinate with Private upgrade team to produce customer release notes and provide assisted upgrade windows for affected customers
rollback_plan: If tokens/sec or TTFT regress beyond acceptable thresholds in canary, immediately revert canary nodes to runtime-1.19 and re-route affected tenants to the compat kernel. Notify SRE and customers, and open follow-up investigation.
testing_notes: Perf harness reproduces tokens/sec collapse within 15-30 minutes using customer trace from NovaDocs
Unit tests added for preemption cancel path and scavenger behavior
Added regression assert to perf CI to fail if tail-90 TTFT increases >2x compared to baseline for long-context test
